businessRules.rule: A person is found either by typing a student ID or employee number where the user has it in front of them, or by searching on name, roll number, guardian name or guardian phone. Names repeat constantly, and the guardian phone is often the fastest unique key.

A typed identifier is never silently accepted. The matched person is shown with their photograph, name, father's name, class and section or role, and identifier, and the user confirms before any field is populated. A single mistyped digit resolves to a real record and produces a valid card carrying another child's photograph, and this confirmation is the only thing standing between the two.

Search results are scoped as the global search scopes them, so a user never sees a person they could not open, and are limited to active records by default. A picker returning withdrawn students would allow a card to be issued to a child who has left.
On confirmation the card fields are filled from the record — name, photograph, class or role, identifier and expiry. They are not typed by hand.

Issuing and replacing are not the same act. The first card is free, for a student and an employee alike. A replacement for a lost card is charged, the guardian pays it for a student card, and the replacement generates a new card number and voids the old one.

Three card types are issued here — student, staff and pickup. All three follow the same flow of finding the person, confirming them, filling from a record, previewing, printing and recording the issue. What varies is the type and its source record.
Printing happens only from the preview, singly or as a batch, so the person on the screen is the last thing the user sees before the card is produced.

A pickup card is a bearer card. Whoever presents it may collect the child it names. The school holds no record of who the guardian has given it to, and the guard checks the card and the child rather than the person.
The card carries the child's own photograph and details rather than the holder's, so the guard is confirming that the card matches the child being released.

The guardian requests the cards and the school issues them. The School Admin sets how many a child may have, because every card in circulation is another key to that child and a family holding six has six ways to lose one.

Because the card is a bearer card, voiding a lost one is the only control the school has. A guardian reports a card lost from their own portal and it is voided immediately, before any replacement is produced, and it fails at the gate at once rather than at the end of the day. Until it is voided, whoever holds it can collect the child.
A pickup card is valid only while the child is enrolled. On withdrawal every pickup card naming that child is voided.

Where a person arrives with no card, the release is not left to the guard's judgement. The office verifies against the record and a one-time code is sent to the guardian's registered number, which the person supplies. The release is recorded as verified by code rather than by card, and the two are distinguishable afterwards.

Every collection is recorded — which child, which card number or code, and at what time. The school cannot record who collected, since it does not know, but it can record which card was used and when, which is what allows a family to be asked afterwards who they gave it to.

A voided card is never reactivated. A family who finds a card they reported lost is issued a replacement rather than having the old one restored, because the school cannot know whose hands it passed through in the meantime.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Cards → Issue a card → Find the person
basicFlow.userAction: Finds the person, either by typing a student ID or employee number, or by searching on name, roll number, guardian name or guardian phone.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Returns matches scoped as the global search scopes them, limited to active records.

basicFlow.navigation: Find the person → Confirm this person
basicFlow.userAction: Reads the photograph, name, father's name, class and section or role and identifier, and confirms this is the right person.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Populates nothing until the confirmation is given, so a mistyped digit cannot silently produce somebody else's card.
Fills the card fields from the record. For a pickup card it fills the child's own photograph and details, since the guard confirms the card against the child.

basicFlow.userAction: Previews the card with the photograph and the filled fields visible, then prints singly or as a batch.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Prints only from the preview, so the person on the screen is the last thing seen before the card is produced.

basicFlow.userAction: Hands the card over and records it as issued.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the card number and the date. For a pickup card it records nothing about who will hold it.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Portal → My children's pickup cards → Request a card
basicFlow.userAction: Requests a pickup card for their child.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks how many the child already has against the limit the School Admin has set.

basicFlow.navigation: My children's pickup cards → Report a card lost
basicFlow.userAction: Reports a card lost from their own portal.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Voids it immediately, before any replacement, and makes it fail at the gate at once.
Voids every pickup card naming a child who has been withdrawn.

alternateFlows.behaviour: They search on name, roll number, guardian name or guardian phone. The guardian phone is often the fastest unique key, since names repeat constantly (BR-1).

alternateFlows.condition: The child is already at the card limit
alternateFlows.behaviour: The request is refused, since every card in circulation is another key to that child (BR-10).

The office verifies against the record and a one-time code goes to the guardian's registered number. The release is recorded as verified by code rather than by card, and the two are distinguishable afterwards (BR-13).

alternateFlows.condition: A family finds a card they reported lost
alternateFlows.behaviour: The voided card is not restored. A replacement is issued instead, because the school cannot know whose hands the lost card passed through (BR-15).

alternateFlows.condition: The school needs to stop every card for a child at once
alternateFlows.behaviour: Every card naming that child is voided and the guardian is issued fresh ones. This is the only way to stop a person collecting, since the school does not know who holds a card (BR-8, BR-11).

departures.requirement: No card can be built or printed without the matched person being confirmed. A typed identifier is never silently accepted, because a mistyped digit resolves to a real record and produces a valid card carrying another child's photograph.
There is no route that prints a card without the photograph having been on the screen immediately before.
The system holds no field, anywhere, recording who a pickup card was given to. It is a bearer card and the school does not know.

A voided pickup card fails at the gate within seconds, not at the end of the day, and a guardian can void one from a phone without contacting the school. With a bearer card this is the only control the school has, so it must be instant and it must be easy.
A voided card cannot be restored by any route, because the school cannot know whose hands it passed through while it was lost.
No child is released without a record of which card or code was used and when. The school cannot record who collected.
Cards and collection records are retained 7 years, since a collection record is the only thing that answers the question asked after an incident.

openQuestions.question: How many pickup cards may a child have? Every card in circulation is another key to that child.

A bearer card cannot bar a named person, since the school holds no record of who holds one. In a custody dispute the school can only void every card for that child and reissue to the parent it recognises. Whether that is sufficient for the school's circumstances is not decided.
openQuestions.assumption: Not decided. This is the consequence of the bearer design.

openQuestions.question: With a bearer card the school cannot record who collected a child, only which card was used. Whether that is sufficient is not decided.
openQuestions.assumption: Not decided. The collection record answers which key, not which person.

openQuestions.question: Is a replacement pickup card charged? A lost student card is charged as an administrative cost, but a lost pickup card is a safety matter and charging may discourage the report the school most needs.
Whether a card replaced because it has expired is free, as distinct from one replaced because it was lost, is not decided.
openQuestions.assumption: Charged as modelled for lost only.

openQuestions.question: How long is the one-time code valid when somebody collects without a card?
Gate and entry security has not been written as a feature. Until it is, the card is produced and nothing specifies what happens when it is presented.
openQuestions.assumption: Blocking for the pickup card to work end to end.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
